memory_candidates.content: When a shell-suite fixture asserts on a durable issue-log side effect (issue-record.sh), confirm the suite's sandboxed script-copy set (both the require_file existence-check list AND the cp loop that populates $WORKDIR/.claude/scripts/) actually includes that collaborator before writing the assertion -- a dormant call site elsewhere in the SUT (e.g. MAX_INFRA_FAILURES's own issue-record.sh call) can pass require_file's sanity check while never having been copied into the fixture sandbox, so the FIRST test to actually exercise that call path discovers the gap at runtime, not at review time.

When several plan phases unavoidably land edits in the same shared file (because the phases are genuinely disjoint code regions of one script, not because phase boundaries were drawn badly), true per-phase git history separation is still achievable after the fact: diff HEAD against the final cumulative file, confirm the diff hunks are disjoint by phase (no two phases' edits share a hunk), then reconstruct each phase's own incremental file content via exact string replacement (python str.replace with the same old/new text used for each edit), verify each incremental reconstruction's diff-against-final contains exactly the remaining phases' hunks, and commit each incremental state in turn. This recovers clean phase-scoped commits even when phases were implemented out of git-commit order.
